newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Illovo shares see big foreign buy - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Illovo shares see big foreign buy - dealers.

text.p: A foreign investment worth almost 16.5 million rand was on Wednesday night made in shares in Illovo Sugar, the South African sugar producer which this month bought Lonrho Plc's sugar division, dealers said.
"Stock was bought from a local broker and placed offshore," said a dealer on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.
"It was a straight foreign investment in South Africa."
By 0826 GMT Illovo shares were trading unchanged at 940 cents following the deal in 1.75 million shares overnight.

Illovo announced on May 8 that it had bought Lonrho's sugar unit, which has operations in South Africa, Mauritius, Malawi and Swaziland, for over 1.6 billion rand, creating Africa's biggest sugar group.
Analysts said the acquisition would give Illovo, which has a 44 percent domestic market share, a more strategic position within the regional sugar industry.
"Prior to this deal, Illovo was pretty much focused on Natal dryland cane.
"Whereas buying in Lonsugar they have immediately captured a more secure strategic positioning within the whole southern African regional industry," Investec Securities analyst Carolyn Windsor said.
Illovo shares hit a year high of 990 cents on the day the deal was announced. Dealers said any move down to nine rand would be seen as a buying opportunity.
